'''Makuva''', also known as '''Makuʼa''' or '''Lóvaia''',<ref>{{cite journal |last=van Engelenhoven |first=Aone |date=2010 |title=The Makuva Enigma: Locating a Hidden Language in East Timor |journal=Revue Roumaine de linguistique |url=https://www.lingv.ro/RRL%202%202010%20art05van%20Engelenhoven.pdf |volume=80 |pages=161–181}}</ref> is an apparently extinct [[Austronesian languages|Austronesian language]] spoken at the northeast tip of [[East Timor]] near the town of [[Tutuala]].

Makuva has been heavily influenced by neighboring [[East Timor languages|East Timorese Papuan languages]], to the extent that it was long thought to be a Papuan language. The ethnic population was 50 in 1981, but the younger generation uses [[Fataluku language|Fataluku]] as their first or second language.
A 2003 report estimated that there were only five fluent speakers of the language.<ref>{{Cite Q | Q57377305 }}</ref>
